destination.title: Strong CP: mechanisms, ultraviolet protection, cosmology and tests
destination.question: Which mechanisms can explain, remove or constrain physical strong CP violation, under which symmetry and ultraviolet assumptions, and with what cosmological and observable consequences?
destination.summary: A proposed family covering parity, spontaneous CP, axions, alternative θ mechanisms and their diagnostics. No original region wording was supplied; the scope critique concerns the numerical membership. The proposed organization does not establish any mechanism or quantum-gravity premise.

systems: QCD and extensions with flavour, supersymmetry, mirror sectors or enlarged colour groups
String-motivated effective theories and selected holographic θ-dependent systems
targets: Separation of weak and strong CP violation
Physical interpretation of CP violation and θ dependence
regimes: Source-specific symmetry-breaking scales and cosmological epochs
Ordinary field-theory constructions and conditional quantum-gravity arguments
assumptions: Symmetry protection, gravitational symmetry violation and consistency criteria are assessed source by source.
Different constructions need not share systems, scales, methods or ultraviolet premises.
conventions: Bare θ, physical θ̄, axion expectation values and holographic boundary data are not interchangeable.
Absence of PQ symmetry does not imply absence of axion-like particles.
includes: Axion-quality sources supplied as outside probes
Adjacent CP diagnostics and gauged-symmetry cosmology as explicitly marked overlaps
excludes: Quiver screening without a supplied CP or θ target
Translation-breaking phonons without a supplied strong-CP connection
SPT phase-continuity questions without a supplied CP or θ connection
Universal exclusion or necessity of axions inferred from conditional source arguments

sources.title: Finding the Strong CP problem at the LHC

evidence.text: Can parity-based solutions of the strong CP problem motivate TeV-scale colored particles through Planck-suppressed operators, and what collider signatures and cosmological histories follow?

sources.title: An ultralight pseudoscalar boson

evidence.text: Can a fundamental discrete symmetry produce a two-axion model that solves strong CP, supplies dominant ultralight dark matter with a protected tiny mass, and predicts detectable Standard Model couplings?

sources.title: Fate of global symmetries in the Universe: QCD axion, quintessential axion and trans-Planckian inflaton decay-constant

evidence.text: How can approximate global symmetries yield light pseudoscalars for strong-CP relaxation, dark matter, dark energy and inflation, while controlling explicit breaking, decay constants and cosmological domain walls?

sources.title: Implications of Higgs Discovery for the Strong CP Problem and Unification

evidence.text: Can an exact exchange symmetry explain the small SM Higgs quartic at a high scale, simultaneously support a parity solution to strong CP, and yield precise gauge coupling unification?

sources.title: Gravity safe, electroweak natural axionic solution to strong $CP$ and SUSY $\mu$ problems

evidence.text: Can a gravity-protected discrete R symmetry produce an accidental PQ symmetry that solves strong CP and generates a natural weak-scale μ term despite multi-TeV soft SUSY breaking, while suppressing proton decay and R-parity violation?

sources.title: A Composite Higgs with a Heavy Composite Axion

evidence.text: Can fermionic strong dynamics jointly produce a composite Higgs, break an enlarged QCD color group, and generate composite axions whose enhanced masses remain compatible with solving strong CP?

sources.title: P not PQ

evidence.text: Which parity-based solution to strong CP minimizes the tuning from separating electroweak and parity-breaking scales, remains compatible with collider and flavor constraints, and offers observable consequences of parity breaking and Planck-suppressed operators?

sources.title: Sliding Naturalness: New Solution to the Strong-$CP$ and Electroweak-Hierarchy Problems

evidence.text: Can cosmological survival after the QCD transition jointly select a small nonzero Higgs vev and a small strong-CP angle, without Peccei–Quinn relaxation, and produce correlated dark-matter and EDM signals?

sources.title: Do Minimal Parity Solutions to the Strong $CP$ Problem Work?

evidence.text: Do two-loop threshold corrections invalidate the minimal softly broken generalized-parity solution to strong CP, despite its vanishing tree and one-loop θ̄, and what hadronic EDM pattern should surviving parameter regions produce?

sources.title: Reflections on Parity Breaking

evidence.text: Can exact parity or CP be spontaneously broken consistently with quantum gravity, what protects the resulting domain walls, and what cosmological constraints follow?

sources.title: Neutrinos, dark matter and Higgs vacua in parity solutions of the strong CP problem

evidence.text: Can a parity-related mirror Standard Model solve strong CP while accommodating spontaneous parity breaking, neutrino masses, leptogenesis, dark matter, and collider constraints? How do the conclusions change with the fate of mirror electromagnetism?

sources.title: Heavy axions from twin dark sectors with <math altimg="si1.svg"><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mrow></mover></math>-characterized mirror symmetry

evidence.text: Can a θ̄-dependent mirror symmetry between two dark sectors remove physical strong CP violation without introducing PQ symmetry, while permitting heavy axions and other new particles near the TeV scale?

sources.title: Spontaneously broken (-1)-form U(1) symmetries

evidence.text: Can spontaneous breaking of (−1)-form U(1) symmetry provide a useful account of θ dependence, the Strong CP problem and its known solutions, and suggest viable alternatives based on explicit breaking?

sources.title: Clearing up the Strong $CP$ problem

evidence.text: Does QCD have a physical Strong CP problem, and can ultraviolet P or CP symmetry solve it once theta-vacuum sectors and the distinction between classical, quantum-global and gauged symmetries are treated explicitly?

sources.title: Discrete {theta} Projection: A Gauge-Protected Solution to the Strong CP Problem Without Axions

evidence.text: Can gauging a finite θ-shift, through a compact topological sector, suppress the physical strong-CP angle without a light axion and protect that suppression against radiative and gravitational effects?

sources.title: The EDM inverse problem: Identifying the sources of CP violation and PQ breaking with electric dipole moments

evidence.text: Which CP-violating operator classes can future nuclear, atomic and molecular EDM patterns distinguish, and, assuming a QCD axion, can those patterns identify whether its nonzero VEV mainly reflects high-scale PQ breaking or hadronic CP violation?

sources.title: Quality control for axions and ALPs

evidence.text: How much fine-tuning or ultraviolet protection is required for Planck-suppressed PQ-breaking operators to preserve an acceptable QCD strong CP phase or a specified ALP mass, and what does this imply for dark-matter benchmarks and experimental searches?

sources.title: Planck scale physics and solutions to the strong CP problem without axion

evidence.text: Can axion-free strong-CP solutions using spontaneously broken parity or CP survive Planck-induced symmetry violation, and what upper bounds follow on their symmetry-breaking scales?

sources.title: A Vacuum accumulation solution to the strong CP problem

evidence.text: Can the strong CP problem be addressed without axions by partially lifting θ-vacuum superselection and making small θ an accumulation point of infinitely many membrane-connected vacua?

sources.title: Finding the Strong CP problem at the LHC

evidence.text: Uses the Goldstone boson equivalence theorem for heavy-quark decay ratios. Estimates collider exclusions by combining existing search cross-section limits with NLO heavy-quark pair-production cross sections, including HATHOR in the stable-particle reinterpretation.

sources.title: An ultralight pseudoscalar boson

evidence.text: Use approximate vacuum-realignment relic densities and inflationary isocurvature amplitudes. Add the two dark-matter densities and the uncorrelated isocurvature powers, applying misalignment-angle priors to sketch viable parameter regions.

sources.title: Fate of global symmetries in the Universe: QCD axion, quintessential axion and trans-Planckian inflaton decay-constant

evidence.text: Define PQ charges through the lowest relevant interactions: a singlet–heavy-quark Yukawa coupling for KSVZ, or singlet–Higgs and Yukawa terms for DFSZ. Photon couplings are obtained from model-dependent anomaly charges with a chiral contribution subtracted.

sources.title: Implications of Higgs Discovery for the Strong CP Problem and Unification

evidence.text: Integrates out H′ at tree level in the most general renormalizable exchange-symmetric two-doublet potential. Studies how extra scalar couplings spoil the link between tuning the light Higgs mass and suppressing its quartic.

sources.title: Gravity safe, electroweak natural axionic solution to strong $CP$ and SUSY $\mu$ problems

evidence.text: Using imported anomaly-compatible MSSM R-charge assignments, the authors test N=4,6,8,12,24. They enumerate allowed XpYq superpotential operators and inspect PQ violation from their interference with the PQ-preserving superpotential in the F-term scalar potential.

sources.title: A Composite Higgs with a Heavy Composite Axion

evidence.text: Gauged Nambu–Jona-Lasinio modeling introduces auxiliary hyperfermion bilinears, integrates out fermions to obtain a one-loop effective potential, and studies gap equations using matrix diagonalization and numerical solutions.

sources.title: Strong-$CP$ with and without gravity

evidence.text: Does coupling QCD to gravity turn strong CP from a naturalness puzzle into a consistency condition requiring an exact axion mechanism, and can a gauge formulation protect that mechanism without a global Peccei–Quinn symmetry?

sources.title: Planck scale physics and the Peccei-Quinn mechanism

evidence.text: Can the Peccei–Quinn mechanism naturally solve the strong-CP problem when Planck-scale physics induces explicit global-symmetry breaking, and how would such breaking change axion phenomenology?

sources.title: Solving the Strong CP Problem with Supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can spontaneous CP breaking generate an order-one CKM phase through radiative effects while supersymmetric non-renormalization protects the strong CP phase, and can that protection survive realistic supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: Is CP a gauge symmetry?

evidence.text: Can four-dimensional CP arise as a discrete gauge symmetry after compactification, protecting a spontaneously broken CP solution to the strong CP problem against possible quantum-gravitational violations of global symmetries?

sources.title: Snowmass White Paper: Strong CP Beyond Axion Direct Detection

evidence.text: Which complementary theoretical, astrophysical, collider, EDM and lattice-QCD programs can clarify or test strong-CP solutions beyond developing new direct axion-dark-matter searches?

sources.title: Solving the supersymmetric CP problem with Abelian horizontal symmetries

evidence.text: Can Abelian horizontal symmetries that align quarks and squarks also suppress dangerous supersymmetric CP violation while retaining an order-one CKM phase, realistic quark hierarchies and a viable μ term?

sources.title: Modular invariance and the QCD angle

evidence.text: Can spontaneously broken CP and modular invariance explain a large CKM phase while keeping the physical QCD angle zero, reproduce fermion flavour data, and remain viable after heavy thresholds, supergravity, and supersymmetry-breaking corrections?

sources.title: Strong CP and SUZ$_{2}$

evidence.text: Can supersymmetry stabilize the symmetry-breaking scales introduced by Z2 solutions to strong CP while preserving their protection of the QCD vacuum angle?

sources.title: Solving the strong CP problem in string-inspired theories with modular invariance

evidence.text: Can a modular-invariant strong-CP solution accommodate the mostly positive quark modular weights and nonconstant gauge kinetic functions suggested by string compactifications, while generating a large CKM phase? What follows for gauge unification?

sources.title: High-Quality Axions in a Class of Chiral U(1) Gauge Theories

evidence.text: Can chiral U(1) gauge theories produce accidental axions whose explicit symmetry breaking is sufficiently suppressed for quintessence, fuzzy dark matter, or a solution to the strong CP problem?

sources.title: Holographic Theories at Finite θ-Angle, CP-Violation, Glueball Spectra and Strong-Coupling Instabilities

evidence.text: How does a finite UV θ-angle affect holographic vacuum solutions, spin-0 and spin-2 glueball spectra, stability and CP-violating interactions? Does the imposed vanishing of the bulk axion in the IR suppress physical CP violation?

sources.title: Reflections on Parity Breaking

evidence.text: What cosmological consequences follow if parity or CP is a fundamental gauge symmetry broken spontaneously at low energy?

sources.title: Do We Live in the Swampland?

evidence.text: If ordinary QCD axions are disfavored, can spontaneous breaking of an exact CP symmetry solve strong CP in a quantum-gravity completion? The paper nominates existing models for further embedding studies.

sources.title: A Proof of the Axion?

evidence.text: Does adopting the de Sitter quantum-breaking exclusion criterion force QCD's strong-CP angle to become unphysical through the Peccei–Quinn axion mechanism, independently of naturalness or fine-tuning concerns?

sources.title: Challenges for the Nelson-Barr Mechanism

evidence.text: Under what ultraviolet, symmetry and supersymmetry-breaking conditions can spontaneous CP violation implement Nelson–Barr strong-CP protection naturally, while retaining a large CKM phase and suppressing higher-dimension and radiative corrections?

sources.title: Solutions to the strong CP problem in a world with gravity

evidence.text: Which strong-CP solutions survive hypothetical Planck-scale violations of global symmetries, and can gauge symmetries protect the Peccei–Quinn mechanism sufficiently?

sources.title: CP and Discrete Flavour Symmetries

evidence.text: How should generalized CP be defined consistently with discrete flavour symmetries, and how can genuine explicit or spontaneous CP violation be distinguished from complex Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and vacuum phases?

sources.title: Of CP and other gauge symmetries in string theory

evidence.text: Does microscopic string theory forbid explicit CP violation, including possible nonperturbative CP-violating parameters, so that bare θ vanishes and observable θ originates from spontaneous CP breaking?

sources.title: GeV-scale QCD Axion

evidence.text: Can Peccei–Quinn breaking below the QCD scale solve strong CP while allowing a GeV-scale axion, avoiding existing constraints and producing observable hadronic or ultraviolet-completion signatures?

sources.title: Viscosity Bound Violation in Higher Derivative Gravity

evidence.text: Can curvature-squared corrections violate the conjectured KSS bound η/s ≥ 1/(4π), and do violations correlate with bulk pathologies, inconsistent boundary theories, or restrictions on quantum-gravity embeddings?

sources.title: The Viscosity Bound and Causality Violation

evidence.text: Does reducing shear viscosity in the Gauss-Bonnet holographic model eventually violate boundary microcausality, thereby imposing a consistency-related lower bound on η/s?

sources.title: Landscape versus Swampland for Higher Derivative Gravity

evidence.text: Can consistency requirements on holographic boundary theories distinguish negative-cosmological-constant Gauss–Bonnet gravity theories belonging to the string landscape from those in the swampland, and what do these examples imply for viscosity bounds?

sources.title: Holographic Hydrodynamics with a Chemical Potential

evidence.text: How do general four-derivative bulk interactions change finite-chemical-potential thermodynamics, shear viscosity and conductivity, and what happens to conjectured transport bounds?

sources.title: Higher derivative effects on eta/s at finite chemical potential

evidence.text: Does a finite U(1)R chemical potential modify η/s once supersymmetric four-derivative corrections are included, and does it strengthen or weaken violation of the proposed 1/(4π) viscosity bound?

sources.title: The Shear Viscosity to Entropy Ratio: A Status Report

evidence.text: What explains holographic universality of η/s, how do higher-curvature, finite-N and finite-coupling effects violate or preserve the KSS bound, and can microscopic consistency impose a replacement lower bound?

sources.title: Non-equilibrium dynamics in Holography

evidence.text: How do broken translations and chiral anomalies affect strongly coupled transport, and can holographic entanglement constrain de Sitter matter or clarify TT̄-deformed theories?

sources.title: Non-equilibrium dynamics in Holography

evidence.text: Which transport structures survive or arise when a strongly coupled anomalous QFT experiences a strong external magnetic field? The announced calculation probes chiral-anomaly effects on transport, including the viscosity tensor.

sources.title: Higher-derivative holography with a chemical potential

evidence.text: How do non-minimal higher-derivative electromagnetic interactions change holographic current correlators, charged-plasma thermodynamics, viscosity and entanglement when treated non-perturbatively, subject to proposed physical constraints?

sources.title: Universal aspects of holographic quantum critical transport with self-duality

evidence.text: Which charge-transport properties are universal in neutral thermal CFTs holographic to exactly electromagnetic-duality-invariant nonminimal extensions of four-dimensional Einstein–Maxwell theory, and when can curvature couplings modify them?

sources.title: The Shear viscosity of strongly coupled N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills plasma

evidence.text: What is the shear viscosity of finite-temperature N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory at large N and strong 't Hooft coupling, and what might connect this result to its weak-coupling behavior?

sources.title: Viscosity in strongly interacting quantum field theories from black hole physics

evidence.text: Does shear viscosity divided by entropy density have a universal value in thermal field theories with black-brane duals, and could that value bound a broader class of fluids from below?

sources.title: Viscosity Bound Violation in Higher Derivative Gravity

evidence.text: The authors report agreement among four methods: Kubo and stretched-horizon calculations nonperturbative in λGB, plus shear diffusion and sound attenuation poles at linear order. The membrane calculation uses Kaluza-Klein reduction to a generalized Maxwell action.

sources.title: The Viscosity Bound and Causality Violation

evidence.text: Expand the action to quadratic order in h₁₂, Fourier transform as e^{−iωt+iqx₃}, and obtain its radial wave equation. The retarded stress-tensor correlator gives η in the small-frequency, small-momentum limit.

sources.title: Landscape versus Swampland for Higher Derivative Gravity

evidence.text: Survey positive-energy constraints on conformal anomaly coefficients a and c and their application to Gauss–Bonnet duals.

sources.title: Holographic Hydrodynamics with a Chemical Potential

evidence.text: Grand-canonical thermodynamics follows from the Euclidean action, using boundary counterterms or background subtraction. Entropy and charge density follow by differentiating the free energy; the reported entropy agrees with Wald's formula.

sources.title: Higher derivative effects on eta/s at finite chemical potential

evidence.text: Impose an incoming horizon solution φ=fᵛF with ν=−iω/(4πT), regular F, and boundary normalization F(0)=1. Evaluate the on-shell boundary flux with a generalized Gibbons–Hawking term, then take the low-frequency imaginary part.

sources.title: The Shear Viscosity to Entropy Ratio: A Status Report

evidence.text: Use the holographic Weyl anomaly to relate curvature-squared couplings to CFT central charges a,c. At the order considered, R² and Ricci-tensor-squared terms can be removed by field redefinitions, leaving the Riemann-squared coupling in η/s.

sources.title: Universal Bounds on Transport in Holographic Systems with Broken Translations

evidence.text: Which lower and upper transport bounds survive explicit or spontaneous translation breaking, and should conformal sound bounds constrain longitudinal phonon speed or thermodynamic stiffness?

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture, Central Charges and $\eta/s$

evidence.text: Does an assumed AdS weak gravity conjecture constrain higher-derivative couplings sufficiently to enforce the KSS bound at extremality, and how do these constraints interact with holographic central-charge bounds?

destinations.title: Can curvature-squared corrections violate the conjectured KSS bound η/s ≥ 1/(4π), and do violations correlate with bulk pathologies, inconsistent boundary theories, or restrictions on quantum-gravity embeddings?
Does reducing shear viscosity in the Gauss-Bonnet holographic model eventually violate boundary microcausality, thereby imposing a consistency-related lower bound on η/s?

Can consistency requirements on holographic boundary theories distinguish negative-cosmological-constant Gauss–Bonnet gravity theories belonging to the string landscape from those in the swampland, and what do these examples imply for viscosity bounds?
How do general four-derivative bulk interactions change finite-chemical-potential thermodynamics, shear viscosity and conductivity, and what happens to conjectured transport bounds?
Does a finite U(1)R chemical potential modify η/s once supersymmetric four-derivative corrections are included, and does it strengthen or weaken violation of the proposed 1/(4π) viscosity bound?

What explains holographic universality of η/s, how do higher-curvature, finite-N and finite-coupling effects violate or preserve the KSS bound, and can microscopic consistency impose a replacement lower bound?
How do broken translations and chiral anomalies affect strongly coupled transport, and can holographic entanglement constrain de Sitter matter or clarify TT̄-deformed theories?

Which transport structures survive or arise when a strongly coupled anomalous QFT experiences a strong external magnetic field? The announced calculation probes chiral-anomaly effects on transport, including the viscosity tensor.

How do non-minimal higher-derivative electromagnetic interactions change holographic current correlators, charged-plasma thermodynamics, viscosity and entanglement when treated non-perturbatively, subject to proposed physical constraints?

Which charge-transport properties are universal in neutral thermal CFTs holographic to exactly electromagnetic-duality-invariant nonminimal extensions of four-dimensional Einstein–Maxwell theory, and when can curvature couplings modify them?
What is the shear viscosity of finite-temperature N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory at large N and strong 't Hooft coupling, and what might connect this result to its weak-coupling behavior?
Does shear viscosity divided by entropy density have a universal value in thermal field theories with black-brane duals, and could that value bound a broader class of fluids from below?

sources.title: Building a Holographic Superconductor

evidence.text: Compute zero-spatial-momentum conductivity from an Ax perturbation with e^{-iωt} dependence and ingoing horizon boundary conditions. Use its boundary coefficients for linear response and Kramers–Kronig relations to associate an imaginary pole with a real conductivity delta function.

sources.title: Holographic Superconductors

evidence.text: Solve the fully backreacted radial equations by numerical shooting from a regular horizon, imposing source-free scalar boundary conditions. Compare equilibrium free energies using the regulated Euclidean action with gravitational and scalar boundary counterterms.

sources.title: The dual Ginzburg-Landau theory for a holographic superconductor: finite coupling corrections

evidence.text: Derives the dictionary from asymptotic AdS normalization; extracts boundary falloffs using homogeneous solutions and a Wronskian integral when full analytic solutions are unavailable. Magnetic calculations use Landau-level separation, iterative Maxwell integral equations, and vortex-lattice orthogonality conditions.

sources.title: Building a Holographic Superconductor

evidence.text: Numerically integrate the coupled nonlinear radial scalar and electrostatic equations from regular horizon data to the boundary, impose one vanishing scalar coefficient, and fit the resulting condensate curves near the critical temperature.

sources.title: Holographic Superconductors

evidence.text: Analyze scalar instabilities through regular zero modes. Magnetic separation of variables gives harmonic-oscillator profiles and a Gaussian lowest droplet mode. The neutral instability appendix uses a Schrödinger formulation and Rayleigh–Ritz test functions.

sources.title: Holographic Superconductors

evidence.text: Obtain retarded current responses from coupled linear Maxwell and metric perturbations at zero spatial momentum and their renormalized quadratic action. Extract electrical, thermal and thermoelectric conductivities; use Kramers–Kronig relations to identify zero-frequency delta functions.

evidence.text: Separate scalar waves into spatial harmonics and de Sitter modes, solve the radial equation using hypergeometric functions, impose Son–Starinets infalling conditions, and extract correlators from the on-shell boundary action.

sources.title: Emergent quantum criticality, Fermi surfaces, and AdS(2)

evidence.text: Fermi momenta are located numerically as normalizable zero-frequency Dirac bound states. Feynman–Hellmann-type variations express velocities and residues through bound-state integrals; WKB provides additional asymptotic information.

sources.title: Towards strange metallic holography

evidence.text: Three ultraviolet-completion routes are outlined: F-theory constructions, brane polarization, and a gravitating charged Fermi gas. D0-brane and simple product-cycle Dp examples yield z=2; moduli stabilization is assessed in restricted examples.

sources.title: Holographic Q-lattices

evidence.text: Solve coupled metric, gauge and scalar linear perturbations with harmonic time dependence and ingoing horizon conditions. Extract conductivity from boundary coefficients, fit its low-frequency Drude form and test intermediate scaling through 1+ω|σ|''/|σ|'.

sources.title: Wilson loop calculation in QGP using non-supersymmetric AdS/CFT

evidence.text: Regularize the interaction potential by subtracting the action of two freely hanging strings: E=(S−S_free)/T. For the free-string profile, tune k0 so numerator and denominator zeros coincide, avoiding an unwanted turning point before the IR cutoff.

sources.title: Real time response on dS(3): The Topological AdS Black Hole and the Bubble

evidence.text: Obtain R-current response from bulk Maxwell fields. The temporal eigenfunction expansion must contain both continuum and discrete normalizable modes; functional differentiation of the induced boundary action gives current correlators.
